abstract: Nanopore sequencers have unlocked the potential for a distributed network of DNA barcoding and metabarcoding laboratories. However, the realization of this potential confronts two challenges--one molecular, one computational. First, rigorous indexing protocols are critical to correctly associate sequences with their source specimen or sample; and second, data interpretation often demands processing millions of indexed reads in a structured fashion via complex bioinformatic pipelines. ONTOLOGY addresses these challenges. At its core lies a graphical user interface (GUI) that guides users through the workflow from specimen or sample reception to the generation of DNA barcode records or metabarcode files. To facilitate data acquisition, it includes freeze-dried PCR plates that uniquely tag the amplicons from each well, hence supporting sample-sequence association. The ONTOLOGY GUI is constructed around two core workflows that process data from a sequencing Run. The Barcode Inference Pipeline (BIP) delineates the OTU(s) recovered from each well and designates them as target or non-target sequences via comparison of OTU sequences to a reference sequence library. The Metabarcoding Analysis Pipeline (MAP) processes sequence arrays derived from bulk samples (organismal or environmental DNA) and infers the species represented while rigorously excluding false positives. To validate ONTOLOGY, we present an original data analysis completed via both pipelines. Built for maximum flexibility, ONTOLOGY also supports the analysis of custom experiments. By employing a GUI to coordinate passage through the workflows with structured amplicon tagging and informatics pipelines, ONTOLOGY facilitates the molecular analyses needed to advance biodiversity science via decentralization. Plates and software can be obtained from www.ontology.bio.
